Candidate/race assignments are checked against the retained official county results, not the formerly crossed corpus roster.

sources.speaker: Shannon Portillo
sources.notes: Original forum report names all five candidates and separates District2 from District3. Only speaker-attributed quotations are retained.

sources.speaker: Sara Taliaferro
sources.notes: Original forum report names all five candidates and separates District2 from District3. Only speaker-attributed quotations are retained.

statements.quote: focus on social services in our community
statements.claim: Proposes social-service investment to reduce the need for more jail capacity; expressly criticizes the current expansion project.

statements.quote: we can learn enough that we don’t have to expand the jail
statements.claim: Hopes near-term jail depopulation and learning from pandemic changes can avoid expansion. This is not recast as an unconditional promise never to expand under any circumstances.

statements.quote: bring evidence-based reforms and focus on rehabilitation
statements.claim: Presents research and rehabilitation as the basis for justice policy, rather than treating jail expansion as inevitable.
Presents bringing neighbors together across political divisions as her governing approach.

statements.quote: Economic justice is going to be very important
statements.claim: Emphasizes economic justice and recovery across the community in the pandemic budget context.

statements.quote: we are still asking for their tax dollars
statements.claim: Says the county must support people losing income while remaining sensitive to their tax burden. This does not establish opposition to social-service spending.

statements.quote: that money should be immediately shifted to other resources
statements.claim: Wants money assigned to the jail expansion redirected to other resources, especially preventive services.

statements.quote: I will continue to vote no for jail expansion
statements.claim: Opposes jail expansion, arguing that community investments can make it unnecessary.

statements.quote: Prevention is where our money should be spent.
statements.claim: Prioritizes preventive social services over continued investment in the jail project.

statements.quote: divert people on a more restorative path
statements.claim: Calls for restorative alternatives that keep people from entering jail, alongside housing and behavioral-health support.

statements.quote: maybe save our community from having to pay for a revision and expansion of the jail
statements.claim: By the primary campaign, advocates using the crisis to reconsider expansion and seek alternatives despite her earlier vote for the project. The earlier vote is not substituted for her current stated position.

statements.quote: remaining stuck in that project despite voters’ voices
statements.claim: Frames her challenge around perceived failure to listen to constituents opposing the jail project.

statements.quote: Some of the work I’m most interested in and concerned about is taking a lot of time
statements.claim: Frames reelection around experience and continuing long-term justice and behavioral-health work.

comparisons.analysis: Both support alternatives that could avoid jail expansion. Portillo expressly rejects the current project; Willey frames avoiding expansion as a goal to achieve through near-term depopulation and learning. These nuances are preserved rather than assuming identical commitments.
Portillo emphasizes evidence-based justice reform and rehabilitation; Willey emphasizes bridging divisions and collaborative leadership. Neither is represented as rejecting evidence or cooperation.

Portillo foregrounds economic justice in recovery; Willey pairs support for vulnerable residents with sensitivity to taxpayers' reduced incomes. Both discuss community needs, not a simple services-versus-cuts divide.
Both oppose the current jail expansion and want resources directed toward community alternatives.
Both prioritize preventive or restorative services to reduce jail use. Their separate experiences do not establish an opposing policy on this issue.

Reid firmly advocates redirecting the jail-project funds; Thellman describes reconsideration and an opportunity to avoid expansion. Her earlier yes vote is not used to manufacture an unchanged pro-expansion platform during the primary.
Reid foregrounds responsiveness and change; Thellman foregrounds experience and completion of long-term work. These are actual campaign frames in the correct District2 contest.
